items.title: RSH quarterly survey: repairs and maintenance spending across social housing reaches £9.7 billion in 12 months
items.summary: As reported by GOV.UK, the Regulator of Social Housing's quarterly survey shows repairs and maintenance spend by private registered providers reached £2.4 billion in the quarter to June 2026, totalling £9.7 billion over the past 12 months. Providers raised £4.3 billion in the quarter and forecast £11.1 billion of repairs spend over the next year.

items.title: Thursday Housing Update 25: what happens when the estimated cost of repairs is wrong
items.summary: As reported by consultant lawyer Steve Cornforth, his weekly update for housing conditions practitioners discusses a claim reallocated from the Small Claims Track to the Fast Track after a defendant's estimated cost of repairs proved inaccurate at allocation. It also reviews when a landlord may obtain forced access for an inspection, drawing on the county court decision in Stonewater Ltd v Harris.

items.title: CIH and CIOB publish joint guidance on tackling damp and mould in social housing
items.summary: As reported by the Chartered Institute of Housing, it and the Chartered Institute of Building have jointly published guidance titled Tackling damp and mould: professional practice, cultural change and regulation in social housing. The guide reflects Awaab's Law and the Hazards in Social Housing (Prescribed Requirements) (England) Regulations 2025, and covers construction causes of damp and mould.

items.title: One in four young people use AI to help with their legal needs, Justice research finds
items.summary: As reported by Artificial Lawyer, research by the legal charity Justice and the Administrative Fairness Lab found that just over a quarter of 18 to 24 year olds used AI when facing a legal problem, against around 10% of those aged 55 to 64. Many turned to AI on problems largely outside legal aid, including housing, employment and debt, raising accuracy concerns about unregulated chatbot advice.

items.title: Pennycook praises Supreme Court judgment on Right to Manage
items.summary: As reported by Inside Housing, the Supreme Court has handed down a Right to Manage ruling that housing minister Matthew Pennycook has praised, and which lawyers believe will make it much harder for landlords to object to such claims. The decision affects how and when leaseholders of a qualifying building can take over its management from their landlord.

items.title: High Court ruling on council housing duty will 'influence homelessness decision-making for years to come'
items.summary: As reported by Inside Housing, the High Court has ruled that a local authority's main housing duty does not automatically end once it offers private rented accommodation, a judgment welcomed by the Waltham Forest council involved. Commentators expect the ruling to influence homelessness decision-making for years. It is relevant to solicitors advising applicants in such cases.

items.title: New statutory temporary accommodation duty comes into force
items.summary: As reported by Inside Housing, a new statutory duty came into force on 1 September 2026 requiring local authorities to notify education settings, GP practices and health visiting teams when a child is placed into temporary accommodation. The measure alerts the support services a child needs to their placement. Councils and advisers working with homeless families are affected.

items.title: Consumer upgrades for two housing associations
items.summary: As reported by GOV.UK, the Regulator of Social Housing upgraded Livin Housing and Community Gateway from C2 to C1 consumer grades in judgements published on 26 August 2026. The regulator also graded Amplius Living C2, G1 and V2, noting weaknesses in its repairs service and challenges in meeting the increased legal requirements for tackling damp and mould under Awaab's Law.

items.title: Misuse of AI - Warning notice
items.summary: A warning notice reminds firms and solicitors that they remain accountable for AI outputs, including accurate citations and client confidentiality, as reported by the Solicitors Regulation Authority.

items.title: Awaab's Law Phase 2: Guidance for social housing landlords
items.summary: Guidance for social landlords on Phase 2 of Awaab's Law, extending significant-hazard duties to seven further hazard groups from 30 November 2026, as reported by GOV.UK.

items.title: Superior Landlord Liability, Damp and Mould Claims and Fitness for Human Habitation
items.summary: As reported by Swinburne Maddison, a County Court judgment in Kemp v Henderson Property Management Solutions Ltd, on 15 July 2026, awarded more than £39,000 against the immediate landlord and over £10,000 against the superior landlord for damp and mould and unfitness for human habitation. The note highlights that a claim can succeed on strong documentary evidence without expert surveyor evidence.

items.title: Joseph Harvey & Anor v Polly Louise Heaver & Anor
items.source: Find Case Law, The National Archives
items.summary: The High Court found a let property unfit for human habitation under section 9A of the Landlord and Tenant Act 1985 and ordered specific performance, as reported by Find Case Law at The National Archives.
